flagged.title: Context: WWI & the Western Front
flagged.reason: The video features the fabricated quotation 'It's the only way to forget' on slide and in voiceover, which would penalise students in a closed-book GCSE English Literature exam.

mark_affecting.quote: "It's the only way to forget." / 'Stanhope says, "It's the only way to forget." He's talking about his heavy, heavy reliance on alcohol.'

flagged.title: Act 1: Arrival in the Trenches
flagged.reason: The video includes a fabricated and misattributed quotation ('How awfully nice — if the Dosch didn't tell — and Dosch didn't know') presented as Raleigh's words in Act 1, which would directly lose marks in an exam.

mark_affecting.quote: How awfully nice - if the Dosch didn't tell - and Dosch didn't know

flagged.title: Act 2: Tensions & the Raid
flagged.reason: The video features fabricated or misattributed key quotations on major quote slides ('I'd rather spare you than any of them' and 'The best company commander in the battalion'), states Stanhope objects to sending Osborne rather than Raleigh, and incorrectly sets Osborne reading Alice in Wonderland with Raleigh on the night before the raid instead of Act 3 Scene 1.

mark_affecting.quote: “I'd rather spare you than any of them.”
desperately objecting to sending Osborne out there
“The best company commander in the battalion.”
it's the ominous night before they might die, and Osborne and Raleigh are just sitting in the dugout. And what does Osborne do? He reads Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

flagged.title: Act 3: The Raid, Death & the Ending
flagged.reason: The video presents and tells students to analyze a completely fabricated quotation ('It's just the light — it's nearly morning') and invents a deathbed scene where Stanhope holds Raleigh's hand as he dies, which would penalise GCSE English Literature students quoting it.

mark_affecting.quote: It's just the light - it's nearly morning... quietly replies, 'It's just the light, it's nearly morning.' You absolutely have to unpack the double meaning of this line for your notes

flagged.title: Character Analysis
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly attributes Hardy's earwig races to Osborne (F7), which introduces a factual error in AO1 textual knowledge.

mark_affecting.quote: he even organizes something as trivial as earwig races just to keep morale up

flagged.title: Setting, Staging & Dramatic Techniques
flagged.reason: The video repeats the stale claim that Hardy says 'Cheero' after describing devastating casualties, which misrepresents the text and sequence of the play and would cause students to lose marks on textual analysis and lesson practice questions.

mark_affecting.quote: Like when Hardy gives a casual 'Cheero' right after describing the devastating losses the previous company suffered?
